body:
WHAT
Both the app and the engine decide whether an OpenAI-compatible connection may run without an API key, using the same host rules: localhost and *.localhost, *.local, ::1, 0.0.0.0, host.docker.internal, 127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x and 172.16–31.x. The two copies are separate files because the app cannot import the engine.

WHY
When the engine only knew loopback, a keyless LAN endpoint the app accepted made the engine refuse to boot with 'No API key found'.

WHERE
engine/core/src/config/providerFactory.ts — export function isLocalBaseUrl(url), used by endpointSpecFromSettings (numCtx only for local) and by engine/host/src/bootstrap.ts (`isLocalEndpoint` gate before MissingApiKeyError). app/main/config.js — function isLocalBaseUrl(baseUrl), used by app/main.js hasCredentials() and by app/main/connection.js testEndpoint()/discoverContextLimit().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. For each of http://localhost:11434/v1, http://127.0.0.1:1234, http://192.168.1.20:1234/v1, http://10.0.0.5/v1, http://172.16.0.9/v1, http://172.31.255.1/v1, http://gpu-box.local:8080/v1, http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1, http://[::1]:8000 and http://0.0.0.0:8000, both isLocalBaseUrl implementations return true.
2. For https://api.example.com/v1, http://172.32.0.1/v1, http://172.15.0.1/v1, http://11.0.0.1 and http://mylocalhost.com, both return false.
3. Both return false for an unparseable string such as 'not a url' without throwing.
4. Parity: over a fixed list of ~30 hosts the app's and the engine's functions return identical booleans (this is the assertion the prose says is currently missing).
5. Given settings { provider: 'openai-compatible', baseUrl: 'http://192.168.1.20:1234/v1' } and no key anywhere, hasCredentials(workspace) is true in the app and bootstrapEngine does not throw MissingApiKeyError.
